text: I am at the integration bench. The ticket queue has fourteen open items and I am starting with the disk alert.
I am on the same bench. Tomorrow is my last day in the seat. Today is the handover, between the ordinary tickets.
Then we do the tickets as they come, and you point at the shelf when we reach it. Coffee is on if you want it.
Coffee later. The disk alert is the volume that holds the nightly copy. It is at eighty percent. I am not expanding the volume this morning.
I cleared the old installers off that volume last month. I will look again after lunch. I am not deleting a log to make the graph prettier.
Agreed. Next ticket is a password reset for a clerk on the second floor. I sent the temporary and closed the ticket.
I saw the close. The clerk has to change it at the next sign-in. I am not keeping the temporary on a sticky note.
The sticky notes on this monitor are from a reboot last week. I am throwing out the ones that say done.
Leave the one about the badge printer. That ribbon is still on order.
Badge printer ribbon, still on order. I am not chasing the vendor from this chat.
VPN dropped for the records floor for four minutes. It is back. I did not restart their switch.
I saw the same blip. My session stayed up. If it drops again I will note the time and leave the switch alone.
Monitor at the bench flickers when the heater fan starts. I am moving the cable off the heater. That is the whole fix I am willing to do.
I moved it. The flicker stopped. Do not order a monitor for a cable that was touching a fan.
Keyboard on the spare laptop sticks on the space bar. I swapped in the keyboard from the drawer.
The drawer keyboard works. I put the sticky one in the repair bin with a tag.
A certificate reminder popped for a test host. The date on the reminder is next month. I snoozed it. I am not renewing it from a chat.
Snooze is fine. Put the reminder on the handover list as a date, not as a task I finished.
Listed. Next is the backup window. It ran at the usual hour. The report says completed. I opened the report and did not rerun it.
If the report says completed, leave the job. I am not starting a second copy because the graph looks quiet.
The lab machine under the bench is powered and idle. Nobody is on it. I am not imaging it today.
The 2019 page is still linked from the first-week list. The title on it is Canonical instant for every feed. Wes Calder wrote it. I am not taking the link down.
I opened the link so I would know which page you mean. I am not writing a sunset under it, and I am not putting a banner on it.
The three logs do not share a clock. The page still claims they do. I will not say what a screen should use. Do not write that sentence into the handover as if I had said it.
I will not say what a screen should use. The link stays. I am going back to the disk alert after this.
Good. The disk alert can wait until after lunch if the percent does not climb. It was eighty, not full.
A clerk on four wrote that the hallway printer is out of staples. I am walking a box down. This is not a log problem.
I will watch the queue while you are on four. If a page fails I will leave it in the hold, not delete it.
Back. Staples are in. The printer's display is boring again. Two tickets came in while I was gone, both password resets.
I took one reset. The other is still assigned to the queue. The user is a night clerk who is not awake. Leave it.
Left. Lunch is the usual half hour. I am eating at the bench because the handover folder is open.
I am eating too. The folder has a divider for links, a divider for phones, and a divider for the service cards. I am not signing any of them at the table.
Then we eat. The heater is loud. I am not moving the bench to get away from it.
After lunch I want the phone rows in front of us, then the service card, then we go back to tickets. Ordinary tickets are still the day.
A ticket just landed about a mouse that double-clicks. I told them to try the spare mouse on the hook. I am not replacing a port for a double-click.
Spare mouse is the right first step. If they write again, it can be tomorrow's queue, and tomorrow I am packing.
Noted. The on-call phone for the bench is charged. I put it back on the dock.
The dock light is amber, then green. It is charging. Leave it.
I labeled a cable under the desk because two of them were the same gray. The label says bench, not a system name.
Labels that say bench are enough. I am not renaming a host to match a piece of tape.
Phone rows, then. I have the channel log and a payer filing on the other screen. I am looking, not editing.
Phone rows are in two shapes. The digits form I keep seeing is 6045552701. The dashed form is 604-555-2701. Old rows were not rewritten.
I can see both shapes. 6045552701 is on the older rows. 604-555-2701 is on later ones. I am not choosing a shape, and I am not padding the old rows with dashes.
Leave them. A search will find both shapes. That is the handover. It is not a cleanup, and I am not running a rewrite on the way out.
I will not run one after you go, on the strength of this chat. The rows stay as they are stored. Back to the queue?
Back to the queue. There is a ticket about a shared mailbox that is full of automatic replies. I raised the quota by a small step and stopped.
I saw the quota change. I am not exporting the mailbox to a spreadsheet to count the replies.
The replies are from a form that fires twice. I noted it. I am not rewriting the form today.
A monitor on the far bench went to sleep and would not wake. I pressed a key. It woke. No ticket after that.
If it happens again, swap the cable before you swap the monitor. We have more cables than monitors.
The chair at your station squeaks. Facilities can have it. I am not filing that as an integration defect.
Please do not. I will leave the chair for the next person and take the squeak as furniture.
Service cards next, while the queue is quiet.
The service card for northline-assistant-2024 has no owner. The owner line is blank. Riley Chen's name is on the November 2024 ship paper. I am not copying that name onto the card.
I am looking at the card. The owner line is blank. I am not filling it. Use of a panel at the bay is not ownership.
Then the handover is that the assistant has no owner. I am not appointing you. I am not appointing Riley from this chat. The ship paper stays the ship paper.
I will not write a name in the blank after you leave, not from this conversation. The card leaves with no owner. What is the next ticket?
Next ticket is a request to map a drive the records floor already has. I told them the drive letter they already use. I did not add a second mapping.
I confirmed the letter from my session. Same letter. Ticket can close.
Closed. Another one: the scanner on two feeds a folder nobody opens. I am not redesigning the folder. I told them where the files land.
That folder is on the list I already keep. I am not merging it with the three logs.
The three logs stay three logs. Hospital, channel, payer. I am not installing a shared clock across them while I pack a box.
I will not install one either. A command that tries has been rejected before. I am stating the rejection, not a rule for a screen.
Good. Box is half packed. Books on the left, the headset in the bin, the plant is staying because it is the bench's plant.
The plant stays. I watered it. That is not a handover item.
A late ticket: someone wants the guest wifi password posted on the wall. I said no and closed it. The password stays with the front desk card, not on a wall.
I agree with the close. I am not printing the password.
The handover folder is still open. Links divider, phones divider, service-card divider. I initialed nothing.
I initialed nothing. The disk alert is still eighty percent. I will look tomorrow morning when the building is quieter.
Tomorrow I hand you the key to the drawer and I stop answering the queue. Today I am still on it.
Then take the last ticket with me. It is a request to reboot the badge reader. I am not rebooting it at the end of the day. I told them to try the card again.
They tried the card again and it worked. I closed the ticket. No reboot.
Queue is down to the night-clerk password, which we are leaving, and the certificate snooze. I am logging off the bench session.
I am logging off too. The 2019 link is still the link. The phone rows are still both shapes. The assistant card is still blank. I am not fixing any of the three tonight.
Neither am I. Ordinary tickets are done for today. I will see you in the morning for the key.
